history.origins: Yukon is a patience (solitaire) card game using a single 52-card deck, in the Klondike family. Unlike Klondike, it has no stock; all 52 cards are dealt at the start into seven tableau columns, with the top five cards of each column face-up and the rest face-down. It is classified as a half-open packer. The game is documented in references such as Roya's Card Night (2021) and in solitaire literature; its exact origin and the reason for the Yukon name are not fully documented in the sources.
timeline: 20th century: Klondike variant documented as solitaire; no stock, all cards dealt to tableau.

setup.deck: 52 cards. All dealt to 7 columns. No stock.
setup.dealing: 7 columns: col1=1 face-up. Cols 2-7: face-down cards + 5 face-up each.

rules.objective: Move all 52 cards onto four foundations, building each foundation in suit from Ace to King. Clear the tableau by building down in alternating colors and moving groups of face-up cards; only Kings may occupy empty columns.
rules.gameplay: Move face-up cards + all covering cards (no sequence needed). Place on opposite color, 1 rank higher. Reveal face-down cards. Empty columns = Kings only. No stock. Build foundations Aâ†’K.
